'''Syamadas Mukhopadhyaya''' (22 June 1866 – 8 May 1937) was an [[Indian people|Indian]] [[mathematician]] who introduced the [[four-vertex theorem]] and [[Mukhopadhyaya's theorem]] in [[plane geometry]].

== Biography ==
Syamadas Mukhopadhyaya was born at [[Haripal (community development block)|Haripal]], [[Hooghly district]], in [[Bengal Presidency]], [[British India]]. He graduated from [[Hooghly Mohsin College|Hooghly College]], received his M.A. degree from [[Presidency University, Kolkata|Presidency College]] in [[Calcutta]], and his Ph.D. degree from [[Calcutta University]] in 1910. He also took classes from the [[Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science]].<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=mS9iDwAAQBAJ&dq=Syamadas+Mukhopadhyaya+student&pg=PA4 History of the Calcutta School of Physical Sciences]</ref>

Mukhopadhyaya was appointed by [[Ashutosh Mukherjee|Asutosh Mookerjee]] as professor of mathematics in the [[Rajabazar Science College]], [[University of Calcutta]].<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=q8H3CwAAQBAJ&dq=Syamadas+Mukhopadhyaya+student&pg=PT363 Sources in the Development of Mathematics: Series and Products from the Fifteenth to the Twenty-first Century]</ref> [[Jacques Hadamard]] communicated with Mukhopadyaya about the latter's work on the geometry of a plane arc<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=TBvOAAAAMAAJ&q=Syamadas+Mukhopadhyaya+student Collected geometrical papers of Syamadas Mukhopadhyaya, Volume 1]</ref> and [[Wilhelm Blaschke]]'s book on geometry had a reference to Mukhopadhyaya.<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=oF0eAQAAIAAJ&q=Mukhopadhyaya Calcutta Review 1934]</ref>

He worked at [[Bangabasi College]] and then at [[Bethune College]] in Calcutta, where he lectured in [[Mathematics]], [[English Literature]], and [[Philosophy]]. In 1932, he was elected president of the [[Calcutta Mathematical Society]]. He served in this capacity until his death from [[heart failure]] in 1937. Mukhopadhyaya went to Europe on a Ghose Travelling Fellowship in 1933 to study methods of education. He gave lectures in Paris University.<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=P54UAAAAIAAJ&q=Syamadas+Mukhopadhyaya+student The Mathematics Student, Volumes 1-4, 1933]</ref>
